review: If doing internet research on dark subject matter sounds interesting to you, give this a try. I've finished it twice over the years.

It's a decent game if you like esoteric trivia and doing research like an online detective. The game loop is couched in a nice Black Watchmen-like wrapper to give it a bit of theme and if you enjoy any of that, this game is likely for you.

Get ready to get your Google-fu tested, since if you are not British/American, you will probably have hard time knowing what the puzzles are asking from you. The visuals are nice, but I couldn't lose myself in narrative and the illusion felt flat for me.

If you like games with a minimal ARG interface, while providing a little challenge, This is the one for you. However, the resolution can be terrible at times without proper configuration, but can be pretty as well. There's not a lot of variety in music, which kind of annoyed me by the time I got to the end. Some of the puzzles were difficult, as some of these clues. The story is a little intriguing, but a lack of lore variety besides text drops leaves me wanting. 
Overall, it was an interesting time-waster, and I had a little fun. But make sure to space your time between sessions to maintain interest.
These are all personal opinion, so take my word with a grain of salt. I'm not an ARG professional, just a fan.

Que j'aurais aimé pouvoir conseiller ce jeu ! Quelle frustration de ne pas pouvoir le faire ! Mais il faut bien admettre que nous avons ici un pur chez d'oeuvre esthétique et de complexité qu'il convient de ne surtout pas recommander, afin d'éviter à la majeure partie des joueurs francophones d'acheter un titre qu'ils n'ont quasiment aucune chance de finir (voire même commencer).

A lire comme ça, on peut peiner à comprendre pourquoi je ne le conseille pas vu ses qualités, tout en insultant la plupart des joueurs francophones. Mais je vous rassure ici, je n'ai fait aucune erreur, ni de perception d'intérêt du jeu, ni de considération à l'égard de mes "lecteurs" : ce jeu est assurément très original, mais j'ai acquis la certitude en quelques minutes que ce titre propose un challenge littéralement hors de portée.

N'étant pas familier au genre de l'ARG (que j'ai découvert en jouant à ce jeu), l'Alternate Reality Game, j'ai eu du mal à réaliser que ce que je faisais était bon : avec extrêmement peu d'indices à l'écran, il faut quitter le jeu pour se lancer dans une véritable investigation sur Internet, dans les encyclopédies et autres sources d'informations, afin de trouver un élément commun à des éléments qui semblent n'en avoir aucun ...

... Il faut noter les textes écrits, capturer les photos affichées, utiliser les fonctions de recherche inversée d'image ou parcourir des pages de documents glanés sur d'obscurs sites, pour réussir le tour de force de trouver quelque chose qui puisse répondre aux critères. Et si l'esthétique est magnifique, fluide et originale, elle contribue à perdre d'autant plus le joueur qui aura du mal à comprendre quoi faire de son résultat, et où et comment le valider dans le jeu.

Du haut de mes 18 minutes de jeu, on peut dire que j'ai facilement passé 4 heures sur Internet en recherches diverses acharnées. Après avoir réussi à répondre aux deux "énigmes", il a fallu en résoudre une troisième reliant les deux résultats, sans que rien ne soit clairement dit à ce sujet, ... avant de découvrir, via le trophée Steam gagné, qu'il ne s'agissait ici que du didacticiel ! Opaque, extrêmement peu intuitif, ce petit jeu a tout pour divertir les rares initiés au genre, tout en laissant la majorité des joueurs sur le carreau.

Et pour ne rien ôter à la difficulté déjà présente, l'ensemble est en anglais uniquement. Mais pas un anglais habituel rencontré dans les jeux lambda, non ! D'un très haut niveau linguistique, il est poétique, joue sur les mots avec tant de finesse que même les anglophones peinent à trouver les solutions dans leur propre langue. Autant dire que les joueurs francophones vont rapidement lâcher l'affaire ! Et pourtant, qu'est-ce que j'aimerais essayer de relever un challenge similaire, mais en français ! Lorsque le jeu s'est révélé dans la suite de ses énigmes encore plus tordues, j'ai décidé d'abandonner.

Ahnayro: The Dream World est un pur OVNI, à l'arrière goût d'énigmes à la "Bue Ice" mélangé à "In memoriam". Un pur crève-coeur de ne pas le conseiller, donc. Mais ce choix dépasse les qualités indéniables du jeu, pour ne focaliser que sur la certitude qu'il décevra 99% des joueurs français qui l'essayeront et réaliseront qu'ils l'ont acheté pour rien. J'espère que ce jeu trouvera maints joueurs anglophones qui lui rendront hommage, car je ne doute pas qu'il le mérite. De mon côté, c'est un "non", même si j'y reviendrai un jour. Peut-être.

Ahnayro is a very unorthodox puzzle game. The main gameplay loop consists in the game giving the player a riddle with text and/or images, the player doing out-of-game research on the Internet to figure out the riddle and then inputting their answer in-game. In this sense, it's closer to a sort of single-player ARG or a trivia game than a traditional, mechanics-focused puzzle game like Baba is You or The Witness. 

The aforementioned gameplay loop can be roughly divided into two types of riddles.

The first, which I'll call the "dream world" puzzles, are the trivia analogues - they're riddles about real-world historical events, religious beliefs, literature, (pseudo)science, etc. They're all pretty good: the riddles were only a bit ambiguous on one or two puzzles, and the way you input answers (by picking out "syllables" from a list) makes it easy to know when you're on the right track (if the answer is a French term, for instance, all the syllables are stuff you'd see on related French words). This means that riddles based on stuff I knew something about were easy to get right away, while riddles about topics I wasn't familiar with took some research, but were straightforward once I was done with it. The research itself was pretty fun - you can do most of it on Wikipedia (though Google and Google Image Search help a lot) and the topics the game covered were all really interesting.

The second puzzle time, which i'll call "waking world" puzzles, are the ARG analogues. As you do the dream world puzzles, you unlock links to real Internet webpages and documents that you have to investigate, and then the game prompts you with a riddle regarding that alternate-reality research. These, surprisingly, still stand up - I played the game 5 years after release and only ran into a single dead link (if you think you've also reached it, [spoiler]the blog was moved from <username>.tumblr.com to <username>-blog.tumblr.com[/spoiler]). I wasn't as excited by these puzzles, but they were all still grounded enough in real life stuff to be interesting.

I think the dream world puzzles aren't gated by the waking world puzzles (that is, you can finish all the dream world puzzles without touching the waking world ones), which is a nice touch. The pages associated with the ARG stuff will all eventually decay, and it's nice that the game is still mostly functional when they do.

Overall, this is a pretty cool and novel game. I had fun and was able to finish it solo, but I could totally see it being a fun party or co-op game, too.

Ahnayro was an absolute delight, and a nice departure from my usual fare.

This game is part Augmented Reality Game, so you will need to use external sources of information to solve the puzzles.  Google will generally find everything you need, and I didn't stumble across any spoilers when I did it.

The game gives you riddles, and you have a web of letters you can connect to make the solution word.  The riddles lead you down absolutely lovely wikipedia rabbit holes, browsing around the interesting information and forgetting what you originally came for.  Most of the puzzle solutions could be found with a low to moderate amount of searching, and you feel quite good for getting the result.  

There were no odd leaps of logic. All the solutions made sense to me, even those I did not grasp quickly.  There were a couple that it totally didn't get, and needed to look up hints for, but were fine in retrospect.  I had just failed to make a connection that was provided to me.

I emphatically recommend this as a good variation to all inclusive puzzle games when you want a break from that format.

I haven't finished this, but probably won't.  For how much the store page talks about "puzzles", all I've seen so far is more along the lines of trivia.  You'll be shown a couple of pictures and some text and be asked to choose some letters from a "sigil" to spell out what the pictures are asking for.  Well, either you immediately recognize what the clues are of and put in the answer, or you just type the clues into google and maybe you read a wikipedia article and then type in the answer.  Perhaps the game gets harder?  But I get the idea that harder would just be more obscure trivia--not things that I would call puzzles, which would require another step once you get the trivia.  I mean to say, using the facts in some clever way to get the answer, not just inputting them directly.

The story isn't very engaging either, perhaps because of the way it's presented with you reading some woman's dream journal and looking at documents from the psychiatric facility she was being treated at.  It's all out of context and just doesn't feel very immediate or real.

I love the Alice and Smith games. They offer a unique universe, where you really feel like you are part of some great mystery. The music, the fantastic puzzles and the lore pull you in, and the real world and the game world slowly start blending together and suddenly it's three hours later and you have 26 browser tabs open and three notebook pages full of scribblings. 

Ahnaryo is like this, although sadly not as effective as the Black Watchmen. Most puzzles were quite easy to solve by just googling the keyphrase of that puzzle. And while I liked the whole clockwork mechanic of the puzzles and enigmas the game pretty much ends without any message or notification. I had to browse around on a forum to find out that I'd completed the game. 

Still, I enjoyed the game. I played this with a friend and we had great fun discussing clues and theories and both hunting around on google, skimming through extensive wikis and finding clues. 7.5/10
Ahnayro is everything I wanted games like Myst to be back in the day. Mysterious, spooky, rich, yet solvable. Highly recommend.

Great intro to ARGs, with progressively difficult but clever puzzles. It will provide hours of entertainment and will make you learn about all kinds of new things. Highly recommended, great value for money. Warning; if you don't like reading or are not willing to learn, don't even bother.

Not going to lie, this game is difficult. The puzzles require you to do outside research and sometimes it seems like they just give you BS hints. This being said, the game sucks you in and finding the answers to the puzzles feels very rewarding. 

I wouldn't recommend it to people that get easily frustrated or people that don't like to read or do research. But if you enjoy random facts and learning weird pieces of information by just reading wiki pages then you might enjoy this. I also enjoyed the external pieces of the game, the websites made just for it , etc.

This game is incredible! I wanted to get into The Black Watchmen but felt daunted. This game seemed like a great primer. I actually had a really fun time doing research and learning about history. If you don't enjoy reading page after page of information (a lot of it I found on Wikipedia) then this isn't for you. It takes a lot of patience and thinking outside of the box. The story was kind of lite and could have used a little more, but overall I really really enjoyed it!

Tips I learned along the way:
1) Reverse Image Search on Google is a great way to find keywords and info.
2) Don't be afraid to go to the forums if you are stumped, they have a great system for nudging you in the right direction without spoiling answers. While this isn't a full ARG, its nice to have community involvement.
3) Answers will vary from super basic ("Why didn't I think of this sooner?!?") to really advanced. Start basic and work your way up from there.

You get to hang out in a dream and research the clues you find using your best Googlefu skills!  Great way to experience an ARG style game as a solo player.  The puzzles, while challenging at times, are fun to figure out.  Cool beans I say!  Cool beans!

The game filters into the black watchmen's universe very well with some characters and organisations that exist there. Would 100% recommend if you like hard puzzles and ARG style of games/ story telling.
